template.name: Mindray Vetus 80 Ultrasound (Class I)
template.desc: Mindray Vetus 80 series veterinary ultrasound (Class I; probes type BF). Converted from the CHS Ansur template “0000-Vetus 80 0000000000 AS-NZS 3551 CL1 EST and PVT DD.MM.YYYY.mtt” (file name) and checked against the Vetus 80 series service manual V4.0 (2025-09), ch. 4, 5.2 and 9.3 (the operation manual in the folder holds only the introduction, so it was not used). One repeated “Protective earth resistance” step left out, the fuller copy kept. Electrical safety to AS/NZS 3551:2012+A2. Changed from Ansur: earth leakage NC 5000, ON 10000 µA (B11.6); Ansur and the service manual (9.3, p.428) both have NC 500, ON 1000 µA (for Jonathan to confirm). Changed from Ansur: applied parts are type BF (Ansur: B), so mains on applied parts is now measured (5000 µA); the manual (9.3, p.431–433) gives probes as type BF. Changed from Ansur: the ESA612 steps follow the usual order (enclosure before earth leakage). Protective earth 0.2 Ω and patient leakage 100/500 µA agree with the manual. Changed from Ansur: the visual, power-on, display and touch screen, imaging, peripheral and battery checks now follow the manual (4.2–4.4, 5.2, 9.3), with labels, fan, date and time, logs, I/O ports and the dead-pixel limits added (4.3.2.2, p.68: no bright or flashing spots, at most 7 dark spots and 2 in the image area, at most 3 adjoining pairs), and “PERFORMANCE TEST” split into the six phantom tests of 4.5.2. The manual gives no numeric limit for the phantom tests, so they are recorded and judged by the engineer. The optional ECG module is type CF in the manual and is not part of this template.

items: Main unit shell and control panel: no cracks, no loose or missing keys, knobs or terminals, no liquid residue, no abnormal smell (scorch, smoke from the air vent), no exposed conductive parts.
Power cord and plug: cord not wrinkled, cracked or aged; plug firm and not loose or broken; the anti-drop hook works.
Labels on the main unit, the general warning labels and the anti-pinch labels are complete and legible.
Probes: head not cracked or swollen; cable not aged or peeling; connector pins not bent, damaged or missing.
Trolley casters: not cracked or skewed; every caster lock locks and releases; base connection screws not loose.
Handles (front and rear): no cracks; the rear handle does not move when pushed and pulled with both hands.
Control panel arm: the panel moves normally, holds its position and is not tilted or loose.
Display support arm: the display tilts, lifts and turns left and right without noise, moves up and down with the arm and stays put when the arm is locked; the display does not lean left or right.
Switch on and shut down: the system starts and shuts down in the normal time, with no abnormal noise or error message; the fan runs without abnormal noise straight after start-up.
Setup > About: the product configuration, software version and loaded options are correct and match the unit; unit details recorded.
The display brightness and contrast, and the displayed date and time, are correct.
The system status indicator is normal, and the log records have been checked with the user for anything abnormal.

steps.title: Mains voltage
steps.instructions: Plug the ESA612 into the mains supply you are testing from.

steps.title: Protective earth resistance
steps.instructions: Connect the device’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet. Clip the red test lead to the protective earth terminal, an exposed earthed metal part (such as a rear-panel screw) or the equipotential pole.

steps.title: Insulation: mains to protective earth
steps.instructions: Connect the device’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet and switch the device on. Don’t touch the device during the test.

steps.title: Enclosure leakage
steps.instructions: Connect the device’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet. Clip the red test lead to an unearthed part of the enclosure.

steps.title: Earth leakage
steps.instructions: Connect the device’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet. The device will be switched on and off between conditions.

steps.title: Patient leakage
steps.instructions: Connect a probe to the unit and clip the ESA612 applied-part lead (RA) to the probe head wrapped in aluminium foil. Repeat for each probe type in use; all probes are type BF.

steps.title: Mains on applied parts
steps.instructions: Probes are type BF: mains on applied parts must stay at or below 5000 µA. Mains voltage is applied to the probe lead during this test: do not touch the probe or the lead.

steps.title: Control panel, display and touch screen

items: Control panel: every key and knob works, checked from left to right and top to bottom.
Trackball: runs smoothly and moves the cursor in the same direction as the ball (try it in Freeze and in Measure).

Main display: the + key raises and the – key lowers brightness and contrast, and the defaults can be restored. Dead pixels on the test screen (Service login, Setup > Maintenance > Setup > Test Main Monitor): no bright or flashing spots; at most 3 pairs of adjoining dark spots and none in the image area; no run of three or more dark spots; faulty pixels at least 5 mm apart.

Touch screen: the function keys respond in B, M, PW, CW and Colour modes; brightness and contrast adjust (+ raises, – lowers) and the defaults can be restored; the same dead-pixel limits as the main display apply (Service login, Maintenance > Setup > Touch Panel test screen).

readings.label: Bright spots and flashing spots on the main display, total (max 0)
Dark spots on the main display, total (max 7)
Dark spots inside the image area of the main display (max 2)
Pairs of adjoining dark spots on the main display (max 3, none in the image area)
Dark spots on the touch screen, total (max 7)
Dark spots inside the image area of the touch screen (max 2)

items: B mode: the B mode key enters B mode; turning the gain knob clockwise raises the gain and anticlockwise lowers it; the image depth changes (the available depths depend on the probe); B then Dual shows two windows with the right image active (press again to switch window); pressing the Quad key four times shows four B images, three frozen and one active.
M mode: the M mode key shows the M-mode image; gain, depth and M speed adjust in real time.
Colour mode: the colour mode key shows the colour image; colour gain, wall filter and PRF adjust in real time.
Power mode: the Power image shows; power gain and power filter adjust in real time.
PW/CW Doppler: the PW mode key shows the spectrum; gain, wall filter, PRF, SV depth and angle adjust in real time (CW only with a probe and board that support it).
Basic measurements: Measure and Caliper enter the measurement modes; a length or an area gives a result below the image in real time; pressing the key again (or Esc) leaves the measurement.

Cine review: Freeze (with Status after Freeze set to Cine) enters manual review; iStation > Review opens a cine file; Auto Play on the touch screen changes the auto review speed (a speed of 0 leaves auto review); Set Begin and Set End on the touch screen limit the replay; Freeze again unfreezes and returns to scanning.
Probe identification: each probe in each probe socket is recognised; after Freeze, removing one probe and plugging in another is recognised immediately.

Image management: Save stores a single-frame image to the animal database and shows its thumbnail; ending the exam sends the images to the DICOM or print server if one is set; Review, iVision and iStation open and close normally.
Scanning each probe: a clean image with no dropouts, vertical bands or artefacts across the whole probe face.

Footswitch (if fitted): connected to the USB port, the right key freezes and unfreezes the image; the other keys do what System > Console&Footswitch says (for example the middle key saves a movie and the left key saves an image).
Video printer and graph/text printer (if fitted): the print key prints an image or report free of defects or degradation (repeat on the other video output port).
Barcode scanner (if fitted): a scanned barcode shows on the screen straight away and matches the barcode.
DVD-R/W (if fitted): ejects, reads and burns a disc without noise.

Video, network and USB ports: an external VGA or HDMI display shows the same picture as the main unit, stable and without colour cast, jitter or flicker; the network connects and communicates; a USB drive stores and reads.

ECG module (if fitted): ECG on shows ECG waveforms and a heart mark, with the respiration waveform at the top right; speed, ECG gain, position and invert adjust in real time; the signal replays properly.

steps.title: Performance test (phantom)
steps.instructions: Phantom KS107BD for low-frequency probes and KS107BG for high-frequency probes. Probe head on the acoustic window with gel or water, no gap and no pressing; display brightness and contrast at the clinical (default) setting; dark room. The manual gives no numeric limit for these tests (the error formulas and figures are images) and says phantom tests are optional in periodic maintenance: record each result in the comments.

items: Transverse resolution (4.5.2.1): focus on the transverse targets and set gain, dynamic range and TGC so only the target line shows; record the smallest separation clearly resolved at each depth.
Axial resolution (4.5.2.2): focus on the axial targets, same settings; record the smallest separation clearly resolved at each depth.

Maximum detection depth (4.5.2.3): maximum display depth for the probe, focus at the deepest point, AP at its largest, raise gain, contrast and TGC without halos or defocusing; record the depth of the deepest clearly imaged target line.
Axial geometric accuracy (4.5.2.4): caliper on the top edge of the vertical targets in 20 mm steps; record the error of the readings that deviate most from 20 mm.
Lateral geometric accuracy (4.5.2.5): caliper on the horizontal targets in 20 mm steps (convex probe: all targets in view at once); record the error of the readings that deviate most from 20 mm.

Dead zone (4.5.2.6): reduce the depth, focus on the shallowest target, lower AP and gain until background noise is just visible; record the depth of the shallowest clearly imaged target (dead zone targets: phantom KS107BD 3–10 mm, KS107BG 2–8 mm).
AC connected and the unit running: the battery is at 100 % or its level rises (below 90 % it should gain 1 % in under 5 minutes; above 90 % it takes longer).
Standby with the AC lead disconnected: the standby indicator shows the unit stays in standby on battery.
The unit runs on battery with the AC lead disconnected.

readings.label: Time for the battery level to rise by 1 % while charging below 90 % (max 5 min)
